findings.body: internal/cli/sandbox.go:114-123 resolves the default tk version with sandboximage.PinnedTkVersion(), which walks up from the cwd to a go.mod and reads image/Dockerfile. It does this even under --declared-only. In a worker container there is no ticfac checkout, so the verb exits 1. image/common.sh:1056 swallows the failure (|| declared=""), and check_declared_image never refuses a mismatched image. Reproduced: a repo declaring [sandbox] image, `ticfac sandbox image --declared-only --root <repo>` run from outside the module gives exit 1 'no go.mod above'. Fix: read the pin from the embedded image/ FS, or skip version resolution under --declared-only, and add a test run outside the module root.
findings.title: ticfac sandbox image needs ticfac's source tree, so the container's declared-image check is always skipped

findings.body: image/worker.sh nudge_due (715-727) refuses a nudge only once the time since the first start has reached harness_timeout. Each nudge then runs under a fresh `timeout $harness_timeout` (823-824) and a fresh omp --max-time. A first run that exits 0 with no report at 0.9T can therefore run to about 1.9T, past the dispatcher bound the variable exists to stay under, and a killed container pushes nothing. This is latent while no caller sets harness_budget_ms. Pass the remaining budget to each nudge, and test a nudge combined with a bound.
findings.title: Worker re-prompts each get a full harness bound, so a nudged worker can run ~2x TICKS_WORKER_TIMEOUT

findings.body: After 46x the image scripts need ticfac, but worker.sh --probe (225-249) and the Dockerfile's green-start layer check only tk, git and the harness. A missing ticfac (exit 127) surfaces as EXIT_CONFIG 'TICKS_SUBSTRATE must be herdr, harness, auto or cloud' (entrypoint.sh:170-173) or EXIT_MODEL 'broken config' (common.sh:222-225), and toolchain provisioning and the image check are skipped silently. Add ticfac to the probe and a verify_ticfac check that names the real cause. This complements finding b87b1159, which is about installing ticfac in image/Dockerfile.
findings.title: A worker image without ticfac probes green, then dies with a misleading config/model error

findings.body: readSandboxTick (internal/cli/sandbox.go:697-711) only JSON-decodes the record. A tick {"id":"a1w","title":"t"} renders a prompt where tk exited 1 because status is required. `--tick ../evil` reads .tick/evil.json and renders branch tick//evil. The code's own comment says booting a worker on damaged state is worse than not booting. Validate the id as a tick id, and the record's required fields, as tk did.
findings.title: ticfac sandbox worker-prompt accepts schema-invalid and path-escaping tick records that tk refused

findings.body: 4i8 deleted TestAnEditedChangelogIsRefused. contracts/CHANGELOG.md and README.md are no longer covered by any digest: only a '## <version>' heading is checked, so a past entry can be rewritten silently. cloudflare/scripts/contracts.mjs still carries the 'pinned' mode and contracts:sync, which fetch all 16 files from ticks, which ships two. cloudflare/CONTRACTS.md:35,114 still documents it. herdr-kinds.md:18 also links a heading (#the-helper-tk-herd) that no longer exists, and references_test.go ignores anchors.
findings.title: Contract changelog/README lost digest coverage and cloudflare contracts.mjs keeps a dead ticks-sync path
